purpose: SC-2 proof: a NON-pivot bar high B*=(16,120) is the canonical all-highs upper-log-hull anchor; a strict k=3 pivot PREFILTER would wrongly select the only k=3 pivot (4,160), whose steeper line is pierced by later highs and does NOT dominate. The all-highs hull selects the non-pivot anchor correctly.

params.eps_break_note: eps_break is illustrative only, never locked (HD-03, §13.5). No breakout occurs in this fixture, so eps_break is not exercised.

expected_second_anchor.reason: All-highs upper-log-hull vertex: shallowest descending line from A dominating every later bar high within eps. NOT a k=3 pivot (H[16]=120 < H[13]=126 and < H[14]=120.5 within k=3), yet canonical per §6/§8 and the 2026-07-25 SC-2 decision (§5).

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(4,160) — the ONLY k=3 pivot after the ATH; what a strict k=3 PREFILTER would pick
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Its steeper line is pierced by later bar highs, so it is NOT envelope-valid. A strict k=3 pivot prefilter (restricting candidacy to pivots) would WRONGLY select this bar (or, treating it as invalid, wrongly emit NO_VALID_SECOND_ANCHOR) and thereby exclude the true canonical anchor at t=16. This is the SC-2 failure the 2026-07-25 decision forbids (§5).

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(13,126) — a HIGHER-priced, earlier bar high
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Although its price (126) is higher than B*'s (120), its line from A is STEEPER (more negative slope) than B*'s, so it is not the shallowest dominating line. A higher price does not make a bar the canonical anchor; the shallowest-slope (upper-hull) bar does.

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(14,120.5) — the HIGHER bar within k=3 that makes t=16 a non-pivot
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: This is the bar that disqualifies t=16 as a k=3 pivot (it is higher and within 3 bars). Yet it is NOT the canonical anchor: being earlier, its line from A is STEEPER than B*'s, so B* (later, slightly lower) gives the shallower dominating line. This is exactly the RM-01 geometry (a higher, earlier bar yields a steeper — not shallower — slope).

rejection_rationale.candidate: B*=(16,120) itself piercing any bar high (validity of the selected line)
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: The selected all-highs hull line dominates every bar high within eps=0.02, so nothing pierces it -> it is the valid canonical envelope.
rejection_rationale.numeric: Tightest downstream margins: t=17 high 114 < line 116.229; t=19 high 106 < line 109.041; t=20 high 102 < line 105.613. All later highs strictly below the line -> 0 pierces.

rejection_rationale.rejected_because: The selected anchor is NOT a k=3 pivot; the only k=3 pivot (t=4, H=160) would give the wrong line (steeper, pierced, non-dominating); the all-highs upper-log-hull selects the non-pivot bar t=16 correctly (SC-2). Pivot detection is secondary/non-authoritative (§5, D-TL-03) and must never change the canonical anchor (D-TL-05).
rejection_rationale.numeric: Pivots after ATH: ONLY t=4 (H=160 > H[1..3]=150,155,158 and >= H[5..7]=158,154,150) is a k=3 pivot. t=16 is only a k=1 local high (H[16]=120 > H[15]=119, >= H[17]=114) but NOT k=3 (H[16]=120 < H[13]=126, < H[14]=120.5). Shallowest slope among ALL later highs is at t=16 (m=-0.0319266, closest to zero) -> upper-hull vertex.

key_inequalities: Anchor A=(0,200): yA=ln200=5.298317. Candidate set = ALL later bar highs (t>0), NOT a pivot subset (§8, 2026-07-25 SC-2 decision).
Shallowest-slope (upper-hull) test over all later highs: slope(A->t) = (ln H[t]-5.298317)/t. Max (closest to zero) is at t=16: m=-0.0319266.
Comparators steeper (more negative): (4,160)->-0.0557859; (13,126)->-0.0355412; (14,120.5)->-0.0361905; therefore none is the shallowest dominating line.
Domination: the A->B* line (m=-0.0319266, b=5.298317) sits at/above EVERY bar high within eps=0.02 -> 0 pierces (t=16 lies exactly on the line).
Non-pivot proof: H[16]=120 is NOT a k=3 pivot because H[16] < H[13]=126 and H[16] < H[14]=120.5 (higher bars within k=3). It is only a k=1 local high.
Only k=3 pivot after ATH = t=4 (H=160). Its line is pierced immediately: y_hat_P(5)=5.019390 < ln158-eps=5.042595 -> t=5 high pierces; P does NOT dominate -> a k=3 prefilter is WRONG.
Conclusion: all-highs upper-log-hull selects the NON-pivot bar B*=(16,120); a strict k=3 pivot prefilter would select the wrong anchor (4,160) or none. SC-2 proven.

pivot_analysis.note: Mirrors RM-01: the upper-log-hull vertex over all highs is a non-pivot bar; the only k=3 pivot gives a steeper, non-dominating line. Pivot status is non-authoritative for selection (§5, D-TL-03, D-TL-05).
